final_result: DATA READY FOR ANALYTICAL TRACK DEVELOPMENT

confirmed_archetype.note: Backend shift-level series are a second, separate measurement scope.

primary_question.target_user: Shift operations manager responsible for staffing and coverage
primary_question.operational_problem: Output per hour and overtime differ by facility and team; managers need to know where coverage review is most needed.
primary_question.question: Across Facility A and B, which team's output per hour and overtime hours differ most from the other groups during 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-28, and how consistent is that gap day to day?
primary_question.decision_supported: Which facility/team to review first for supervisor coverage and overtime allocation (demonstration decision on synthetic data).

tracks.evidence: 6 facility x team groups, each with 5 daily observations of output and overtime (frontend, facility-level); 3 shifts x 7 days in backend. Quality PASS, representativeness PASS.
tracks.missing_requirement: Groups are small (5-7 observations): differences are descriptive, not statistically strong. Compare within a source only.

tracks.evidence: Ordered consecutive daily observations exist, but each series has only 5-7 points over one month (2026-10-24 to 2026-10-30).
tracks.missing_requirement: Fewer than 12 ordered periods; no weekly/seasonal cycle; Last-30-Days and Year-to-Date views are interpolated by the UI, not in the data.
tracks.recommendation: SUPPORTING track, descriptive direction over the 5-7 observed days only. No forecasting.

tracks.evidence: Explainable factors exist (attendance_rate, output_per_hour, overtime_hours) plus a status label (optimal/warning/critical).
tracks.missing_requirement: No documented urgency definition; status thresholds are implicit in UI code; backend status is random and unrelated to its metrics (OBS-3); attendance exists only in backend.
tracks.recommendation: Conditional: only a transparent, rule-based frontend 'coverage review priority' using output, overtime and source-stated status, with documented weights. Not a score of real risk.

tracks.evidence: Largest comparable baseline is 7 observations per series.
tracks.missing_requirement: Needs a meaningful baseline (>= 20 comparable observations); backend values are uniform-random, so extremes are generator noise and cannot be separated from errors.

tracks.evidence: Only 9 entities (6 facility-team nodes, 3 shifts) and 3-4 informative numeric fields.
tracks.missing_requirement: Segments of 6 nodes carry no business meaning beyond the existing team/facility grouping.

No genuine target (status is authored/random label), no real historical outcomes, <=7 observations per series, no validation split possible, no decision-time inputs, high leakage risk (status is a function of KPI in frontend).
tracks.recommendation: Reject. Row count (129) does not justify prediction.

tracks.evidence: No scenario records, no parameter columns, record_type 'scenario' absent.
6 text values, 6 unique, one per node.
tracks.missing_requirement: Sparse, generic, authored insight sentences; no volume for themes.

limitations: All data synthetic; findings demonstrate method, not real operations.
Frontend (facility-level) and backend (shift-level) are different scopes; never pool or concatenate.
5-7 daily points per series, one month only.
Last-30-Days / Year-to-Date UI views are not backed by source data.
Frontend status/KPI/text are authored; backend status is random.
No geography, stages, relationships or scenarios.
controls_for_post3: Read only data/canonical/intelligence_data.csv; filter by source_name first.
Compare groups within a source; report n for every comparison.
Label every output synthetic and descriptive; no forecast, anomaly flag or predictive score.
No second dataset; any canonical fix goes through scripts/data_pipeline with a version bump and Post #1 re-validation.
Do not alter the operational page.
